project_type: .NET 8 WPF worship presentation app (WorshipBacktrackPlayer); multi-project solution: WorshipPlayer.Core (net8.0 class lib), WorshipPlayer.Audio/Presenter/UI (net8.0-windows WPF), WorshipPlayer.Tests (net8.0 xUnit).
build_system: dotnet / MSBuild. Solution file WorshipBacktrackPlayer.sln at the worktree root. WPF projects target net8.0-windows; Core and Tests target net8.0. Build emits a transient WorshipPlayer.Presenter_*_wpftmp.csproj during WPF temp compile — harmless.
test_framework: xUnit (Xunit). Tests in WorshipPlayer.Tests. SQLite tests inject a temp app.db under Path.GetTempPath() and call SqliteConnection.ClearAllPools() in Dispose/teardown so the temp .db can be deleted on Windows.
verification_instructions: 1) dotnet build WorshipBacktrackPlayer.sln must report 0 errors (4 pre-existing warnings are acceptable: MediaLibraryPanel._currentView CS0414, ChordChartWindow CS8604, WaveformEditorWindow._inReviewMode CS0414). 2) Run the relevant test class with dotnet test --filter, then the full suite. All tests must pass. Clean up any temp files the tests create (handled by their Dispose).
snapshot_or_generated_files: None. No committed data corpus to migrate — Songs/ServiceOrders/Setlists are empty and there is no committed presenter-settings.json; a settings.json exists at repo ROOT but is NOT the runtime store and must NOT be touched as data. Runtime stores live under the build output folder (AppDomain.CurrentDomain.BaseDirectory). app.db is created at runtime.
environment_constraints: Windows + SQLite file locks: every SQLite-backed test MUST call SqliteConnection.ClearAllPools() in teardown before deleting its temp folder, or cleanup throws IOException. Reuse AppDatabase (WorshipPlayer.Core/Services/AppDatabase.cs); do NOT add a second db helper. Microsoft.Data.Sqlite only; no EF. bible.db stays a separate database from app.db.
contribution_requirements: Preserve public method signatures and observable behavior (parity migration): SettingsService exposes Settings property + LoadAsync() + SaveAsync(); the new PresenterSettingsService mirrors that shape. Do NOT change AppSettings/PresenterSettings model shapes beyond additive needs; keep them JSON-round-trippable. Enums stored as their string names inside the JSON column. Commit locally on the branch feature/sql-phase04-settings; never push.
key_patterns: Follow SongUsageService.cs as the canonical SQLite store: ctor takes a db path, builds `new AppDatabase(path)`, derives the legacy JSON path as a sibling of the db file, has a `const string CreateSchemaSql` with CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS, an `_initialized` bool guard, `EnsureInitializedAsync()` that runs schema DDL then ImportLegacyJsonIfNeededAsync(connection), a defensive try/catch import that no-ops when the table/row is non-empty (non-duplicating) and never throws on missing/malformed JSON, parameterized SQL via SqliteCommand, and `using var connection = _database.CreateConnection(); await connection.OpenAsync();` per call. MediaLibraryService.cs shows the (string path, string? databasePath = null) two-arg + default-to-AppDatabase.DefaultPath ctor variant. JsonSerializerOptions use WriteIndented = true + new JsonStringEnumConverter().
